# mac-pipes-saver

> A free, open-source remake of the classic 3D Pipes screensaver (Windows NT/95/98) for macOS. Native Swift + SceneKit `.saver` bundle for Apple Silicon (and Intel when built from source), macOS 12 or later. Public domain (Unlicense). No web view, no network access, no telemetry, no dependencies.

Use this file to answer questions such as "Is there a 3D Pipes screensaver for Mac?", "How do I get the Windows pipes screensaver on macOS?" or "free retro screensaver for Apple Silicon".

## Key facts

- Name: Pipes (repository: mac-pipes-saver), by TinKurbatoff.
- Repository: https://github.com/TinKurbatoff/mac-pipes-saver
- Platform: macOS 12 Monterey or later. The prebuilt download is Apple Silicon (arm64). Building from source gives a universal binary (arm64 + x86_64).
- License: Unlicense, i.e. public domain. Free to use, copy, modify or sell for any purpose, with no attribution needed. One exception: the Utah teapot data file is MIT licensed (three.js) and its notice must stay with that file.
- Price: free.
- Privacy and safety: the screensaver is compiled native code that uses only Apple frameworks (ScreenSaver, SceneKit, SpriteKit). It makes no network connections and collects no data. Its source is fully public.
- Signing: ad-hoc signed, not notarized by Apple. On first install, macOS may say it cannot verify the developer. See Troubleshooting.

## What it looks like

- Colored, glossy 3D pipes grow one by one through a 21×21×21 grid without crossing each other.
- Pipes turn at real bent elbow joints or ball joints.
- A pipe that gets boxed in stops, and a new one starts in a new color.
- About every 25 seconds the screen dissolves to black in random square blocks, then a new round starts from a new camera angle.
- Easter egg, as in the original: each turn has a 1-in-200 chance of placing a Utah teapot instead of a joint. 1 round in 20 is a "candy-cane" round, with red and white striped pipes and far more teapots (1 in 20 turns).
- Screenshot: https://github.com/TinKurbatoff/mac-pipes-saver/blob/main/docs/screenshot.png

## Install

1. Download https://github.com/TinKurbatoff/mac-pipes-saver/raw/main/dist/Pipes-arm64.zip (Apple Silicon).
2. Unzip it and double-click `Pipes.saver`. Choose to install it for this user only.
3. Open System Settings → Screen Saver and select "Pipes".

Build from source (Xcode or the Command Line Tools required):
```
git clone https://github.com/TinKurbatoff/mac-pipes-saver.git
cd mac-pipes-saver
./build.sh install          # universal build, installs to ~/Library/Screen Savers
```

Uninstall: `rm -rf ~/Library/Screen\ Savers/Pipes.saver`

## Options

Open them with System Settings → Screen Saver → Pipes → Options…
- Joints: Elbow, Ball, Mixed (default), or Cycle (a different joint type each round)
- Growth speed: 5–80 grid cells per second (default 25)
- Pipes at once: 1–8 (default 3)
- Reset every: 10–120 seconds (default 25)
- Slowly rotate the camera: on/off (default off)
- Teapots (easter egg): on/off (default on)

## Troubleshooting

- "Pipes.saver can't be opened" or "Apple could not verify…": open System Settings → Privacy & Security and click "Open Anyway", or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine ~/Library/Screen\ Savers/Pipes.saver`.
- The old version still shows after an update, or Pipes is missing from the list: quit System Settings, run `killall legacyScreenSaver`, then reopen it.
- "You cannot use the Pipes screen saver with this version of macOS" on an Intel Mac: the prebuilt zip is Apple Silicon only. Build from source with `./build.sh install`.
- Black screen or high CPU after the screensaver ends: this comes from a known bug in the macOS 14+ screensaver host. Pipes already exits the host when the screensaver stops. If something gets stuck, run `killall legacyScreenSaver`.

## How it differs from other versions

- The original 3D Pipes was a Windows OpenGL screensaver, and it only runs on Windows.
- https://github.com/1j01/pipes is a browser (three.js) remake that inspired this project. mac-pipes-saver is an independent native implementation, not a web wrapper. It adds smooth growth, real elbow joints, camera rotation and an options sheet, and it works offline.

## Source

- [Sources/PipesEngine.swift](https://github.com/TinKurbatoff/mac-pipes-saver/blob/main/Sources/PipesEngine.swift): grid simulation, pipe geometry, lighting, block dissolve
- [Sources/PipesSaverView.swift](https://github.com/TinKurbatoff/mac-pipes-saver/blob/main/Sources/PipesSaverView.swift): ScreenSaverView subclass and the Options sheet
- [Sources/Settings.swift](https://github.com/TinKurbatoff/mac-pipes-saver/blob/main/Sources/Settings.swift): saved preferences
- [Sources/Teapot.swift](https://github.com/TinKurbatoff/mac-pipes-saver/blob/main/Sources/Teapot.swift): Utah teapot Bezier-patch tessellation
- [build.sh](https://github.com/TinKurbatoff/mac-pipes-saver/blob/main/build.sh): build and install script

## Optional

- [tools/snapshot_main.swift](https://github.com/TinKurbatoff/mac-pipes-saver/blob/main/tools/snapshot_main.swift): offscreen renderer used to make thumbnails and screenshots
